wiktionary.gloss: A physical, chemical, infective agent aggressing an organism.
Aggression toward an organism resulting in a response in an attempt to restore previous conditions.
The internal distribution of force across a small boundary per unit area of that boundary (pressure) within a body. It causes strain or deformation and is typically symbolised by σ or τ.
Force externally applied to a body which cause internal stress within the body.

examples: Go easy on him, he's been under a lot of stress lately.
wiktionary.gloss: Emotional pressure suffered by a human being or other animal.

wiktionary.gloss: A suprasegmental feature of a language having additional attention raised to a sound, word or word group by means of of loudness, duration or pitch; phonological prominence.

The suprasegmental feature of a language having additional attention raised to a sound by means of loudness and/or duration; phonological prominence phonetically achieved by means of dynamics as distinct from pitch.
Emphasis placed on a particular point in an argument or discussion (whether spoken or written).
distress; the act of distraining; also, the thing distrained.

blocks.etymology: From a shortening of Middle English destresse, borrowed from Old French destrecier, from Latin distringō (“to stretch out”). This form probably coalesced with Middle English stresse, from Old French estrece (“narrowness”), from Vulgar Latin *strictia, from Latin strictus (“narrow”). Displaced native Old English swēġ (“accent, stress”), though strictly in the grammatical sense. In the sense of "mental strain" or “disruption”, used occasionally in the 1920s and 1930s by psychologists, including Walter Cannon (1934); in “biological threat”, used by endocrinologist Hans Selye, by metaphor with stress in physics (force on an object) in the 1930s, and popularized by same in the 1950s.

senses.definition: to give special importance or attention to something you say or write

examples.en: The manager stressed the importance of arriving on time.
examples.vi: Người quản lý đã nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc đến đúng giờ.

senses.definition: to worry a lot about something, or to make someone feel anxious

examples.en: Don't stress about the test, you will do fine.
examples.vi: Đừng quá lo lắng về bài kiểm tra, bạn sẽ làm tốt thôi.

senses.definition: to pronounce a word or syllable with greater force

examples.en: In the word 'banana', you stress the second syllable.
examples.vi: Trong từ 'banana', bạn nhấn trọng âm vào âm tiết thứ hai.

senses.definition: to put physical pressure or force on an object or material

examples.en: Heavy trucks stress the road surface over time.
